about_title:
Vladislav Lyakh.
ML, data & aerial imagery.
about_text: I am a machine learning and data analysis specialist with over 5 years of industry experience. I work across Data Science, Machine Learning and Computer Vision, from framing a problem and preparing data to developing algorithms and checking results.
about_text_2: I apply this approach to aerial imagery: mapping, spatial measurements and image-based object analysis. I work remotely with clients in Russia and CIS countries, communicating in Russian and English.
faqs: What types of project can we discuss?
UAV imagery processing, mapping, area and volume estimation, segmentation, object detection and counting. Custom image and data analysis requirements can be discussed separately.
What input data do you need?

UAV mission images and a short description of the task. Include acquisition parameters, coordinate-system information, RTK/PPK or ground control measurements where available. Start with a few examples; we can agree how to transfer the full dataset separately.
Do you provide drone flights or field surveys?
No. I provide remote processing and analysis. Image acquisition and ground measurements are handled by your team or a separate contractor.

Requirements are agreed after reviewing the source data. Image resolution alone does not establish measurement accuracy. High-consequence applications require suitable georeferencing and independent control measurements.
Orthomosaics or maps, PDF reports, analytical tables and agreed geospatial files. The exact scope and formats depend on the project. This website does not accept large source-file uploads.

No. All four cases are independent demonstration studies using third-party source material. They illustrate processing methods and results, not completed commercial commissions or certified surveying documentation.

projects.title:
A site mapped.
Materials measured.
projects.summary: An orthomosaic, surface analysis and preliminary volumes for three selected stockpile objects.
projects.image_alt: Close view of the mapped construction site and selected stockpile objects.
projects.objective: Describe the visible site surface and estimate the volumes of three selected objects relative to a local reference surface. This is not a complete inventory of the site.
projects.inputs: The report uses 214 aerial images from 11 September 2019 and processed orthomosaic, DSM and DTM products. The horizontal CRS is WGS 84 / UTM zone 54S (EPSG:32754). The vertical datum is not independently confirmed.
method: Map the site and the selected areas of interest.
Inspect surface models, slopes and a comparatively uniform open area, T01.
Define local bases for S01, S02 and S03 and calculate volumes.
Inspect the effect of changing the reference surface and document limitations.
outputs: Mapped coverage: 15.78 ha. This is not the cadastral parcel area.
Three selected objects: S01, S02 and S03; touching piles can form a single analysis object.
Preliminary combined volume: 113.16 m³, conditional on the selected boundaries and local bases.
An 11-page report with maps, object sheets and interpretation.
projects.limits: The source control network does not replace independent checkpoints. DSM/DTM grid spacing is not a statement of accuracy. Some structures and piles may remain in the DTM, so it is not treated as a ready-made stockpile base. Material density is unknown; volumes are not converted to tonnes.
projects.source: Final Construction_Site_Survey_and_Stockpiles.pdf dated 26 October 2026 and original project figures. Imagery acquired on 11 September 2019. Final engineering sheets are used; no new measurements were performed for the website.

projects.title:
A road corridor,
understood in detail.
projects.summary: The visible road footprint, centreline and width variation, with areas requiring additional checks.
projects.image_alt: Aerial view of a narrow road running through a green landscape.
projects.objective: Describe the geometry of the road surface visible within the imagery: footprint, observed centreline and width variation. The analysis does not diagnose pavement defects.
projects.inputs: An existing orthomosaic of the Helenenschacht study area and derived road geometry. The reported extent is limited to the visible imagery footprint.
method: Define the observed road footprint and centreline.
Measure width along the observed axis.
Separate accepted sections, areas requiring review and unmeasured edges.
Report the mapped geometry together with the limits of interpretation.
outputs: Observed centreline: 141.69 m; road footprint: 599.60 m².
Median width: 4.31 m; P5–P95 interval: 3.97–4.84 m.
Accepted length: 112.00 m; review sections: 20.00 m; unmeasured edges: 9.69 m.
A six-page report with geometry, width variation and quality notes.
projects.limits: Absolute coordinate accuracy has not been established with independent measurements. Review areas are not confirmed road defects. The work does not replace engineering surveys, as-built documentation or an assessment of road condition.
projects.source: Final Helenenschacht_Road_Mapping_Report(3).pdf dated 25 October 2026 and original client_delivery figures. The final quality-control map and width profile are used; no new measurements were performed for the website.

projects.title:
Crops and weeds.
From pixels to patterns.
projects.summary: RGB imagery represented as maize, weeds and open surface. A sample-based assessment of eight frames, not a map of the entire field.
projects.image_alt: Two views of one frame: an RGB maize image and its cover-class map.
projects.objective: Demonstrate how crop images can become class maps and quantitative descriptions of cover. Separate crop plants, weeds and open surface within selected image patches.
projects.inputs: Eight RGB patches of a maize field acquired on 6 June 2023 from WeedsGalore. Nominal scale: 2.5 mm per pixel. Additional images from 15 June show different patches and are excluded from the primary assessment.
method: Prepare individual images and visual representations of three cover classes.
Calculate per-image class shares and the aggregate for eight frames.
Show the original image, class map and overlay together.
Prepare a report, keeping the 15 June examples separate.
outputs: Nominal combined area of the eight frames: 18.00 m².
Published sample estimates: maize 3.32%, weeds 5.82%, open surface 90.86%.
Segmentation examples, per-image cover distribution and a seven-page PDF report.
projects.limits: Patch coordinates are unknown. This is neither an orthomosaic nor a survey of the whole field. Areas use a nominal pixel scale. The 6 and 15 June images do not repeat the same locations. Visual examples are not evidence of independent model performance and do not replace field checks.
projects.source: WeedsGalore — Ekin Celikkan et al., WACV 2025; source dataset licensed under CC BY 4.0. Imagery was adapted for this demonstration study; only size and format were changed for the website. Numerical results come from Agro_Field_Monitoring_Portfolio_Final(1).pdf.

projects.title:
Open land.
Terrain and constraints.
projects.full_title: Bellus: open land and terrain assessment
projects.summary: Identify a central clearing, analyse elevations and slopes, and outline preliminary infrastructure scenarios and areas requiring further checks.
projects.image_alt: A Bellus orthomosaic with the central open clearing outlined within surrounding woodland.
projects.objective: Assess the open part of a site for a hypothetical golf-club scenario: where open surface is visible, how the terrain varies, and which areas need ground investigation.
projects.inputs: Bellus demonstration materials: an orthomosaic, derived elevation data and the central-clearing boundary. The client scenario is hypothetical; the analyst did not conduct the aerial survey.
method: Delineate the open clearing while excluding individual visible woody features.
Assess elevations, slopes and longitudinal and cross-sectional profiles.
Compare detailed and generalised terrain views.
Prepare preliminary scenarios and highlight areas needing additional checks.
outputs: Imagery coverage: 25.98 ha; delineated clearing: 2.033 ha.
Cross-slope is the main identified constraint. Published estimates: P2–P98 range 8.13 m; median slope 6.69°.
Elevation and slope maps, profiles and preliminary scenario layouts.
A six-page PDF report for early-stage discussion.
projects.limits: Elevation accuracy has not been independently confirmed. The clearing outline is not a cadastral boundary, and visible open land does not establish suitability or permission for construction. Review zones are not proven defects. Scenario areas may overlap and must not be added together.
projects.source: Bellus_Client_Report_Portfolio.pdf and source figures from the Bellus demonstration study. Website copies were prepared without new surveying calculations. Original acquisition attribution and redistribution conditions still need checking before public release.
